hints: Focus on what type of solution Y makes in water, acidic or alkaline, and what that tells you about Y's position in Period 3.
Notice that X forms an insoluble oxide that can still be dissolved by Y's solution, so X must have an oxide that reacts with both acids and alkalis.
Recall which Period 3 oxide is amphoteric and insoluble, and pair it with a metal whose oxide gives a strongly alkaline solution.
walkthrough:
**Sort Period 3 oxides by acid-base character**

Think left to right across Period 3. Oxides change from basic to amphoteric to acidic.

$$\text{Na}_2\text{O}, \text{MgO basic} \; ; \; \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 \text{ amphoteric} \; ; \; \text{SiO}_2, \text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}, \text{SO}_2 \text{ acidic}$$

**Use the clue about X**

The oxide of X is insoluble in water. That rules out $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$ (slightly soluble), $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ and $\text{SO}_2$ which dissolve or react. It leaves $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ as the classic insoluble oxides.

**Use the clue about Y**

The oxide of Y dissolves to give a solution that then dissolves the oxide of X. Sodium oxide reacts to give strong alkali:
$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}$$

**Match the pair that reacts together**

Aluminium oxide is amphoteric, so although insoluble in water it dissolves in strong alkali:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Na}[\text{Al}(\text{OH})_4]$$
That fits perfectly with X as aluminium and Y as sodium.

options.A: X is aluminium, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble in water but amphoteric. Y is sodium, $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ dissolves to form $\text{NaOH}$, a strong alkali which dissolves amphoteric $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$. Both conditions are met.
options.B: Magnesium oxide, $\text{MgO}$, is basic and essentially insoluble, but it is not amphoteric. It will not dissolve in $\text{NaOH}$ solution formed from sodium oxide, so the second condition fails.
options.C: Silicon dioxide, $\text{SiO}_2$, is insoluble and acidic. Phosphorus oxide gives an acidic solution ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$). An acidic oxide does not dissolve in an acid, so Y's solution cannot dissolve X.
options.D: Silicon dioxide, $\text{SiO}_2$, is insoluble and acidic. Sulfur oxides give acidic solutions ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$ or $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$). Again, acid will not dissolve an acidic oxide, so this pair fails the final test.
